question: The French Ministry of the Interior’s annual report, which was recently published on 25 January 2024, reveals new trends in visa and residence permit applications in overseas territories. Although the total number of residence permits has remained the same, there has been a significant increase in tourist and humanitarian visas and a decrease in student and family visas.

Furthermore, there are regional disparities with regard to asylum applications, with a marked increase in French Guiana and a decrease in Mayotte, indicating that there are new migration routes to Europe. What is the Commission's opinion on these changes in visa and migration practices, particularly with regard to the French Overseas Territories?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (22.7.2024) According to article 138 of the Convention implementing the Schengen Agreement1, the Schengen acquis shall apply only to the European territory of the French Republic. These provisions exclude the French non-European outermost regions which fall under the scope of application of article 349 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union.

Therefore, the Schengen rules are not applicable in Martinique, Mayotte, Guadeloupe, French Guiana Réunion and Saint-Martin. Access to these territories by third-country nationals is not regulated at EU level and overseas visas issued to access these territories therefore fall solely under the competence of the French authorities.

The Commission has not been informed by the French authorities of the mentioned report. As this matter falls directly under the competence of the French national authorities, the Commission recommends that any inquiries or concerns regarding these statistics be directed to the relevant French authorities.
